text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- United Nations envoy on Cyprus Gustave Feissel believes the two leaders on the divided island are ready to sit at direct talks.
- Parliament approves regulations on mergers and acquisitions on the Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE)
- Attorney General Alecos Markides expresses shock at the deportation of a retired British woman allegedly caught working illegally.
- The occupied areas of Cyprus have become a gambling mecca for Turkish gamblers, with Kyrenia boasting the largest casino in Europe, according to a European newspaper report.
- Cattle breeders protest at the presidential palace.
- Outgoing chairman of the right-wing Democratic Rally Yiannakis Matsis dismisses suggestions he is quitting politics.

- Centre-right Democratic Party chairman and former President Spyros Kyprianou warns there will be a split in the government partnership if talks start with the Turkish Cypriot side without common ground being found on basic issues first.
- The threshold of the inheritance tax is reduced, exempting property worth up to 150,000 pounds ($298,000)
- The foreign minister's family firm has been allowed to bend the rules on building permits for their hotels on numerous occasions. ($=0.503 pounds)
